name: A Tale for Wisp
summary: A grey cat in the library speaks with a stolen man's voice and wants stories in his books.

stages.journal: A grey cat sits on the library desk with a stack of books beside him. He speaks in a man's voice, charming and warm, and he wants us to tell him a tale.
objectives: Decide whether to tell the cat a tale
stages.hint: Talk to the grey cat in the library.

stages.journal: We turned the cat down and went about our business. He is still in the library, smiling.
We have told the cat a tale and he wrote it in a book, in words and pictures. He would like another.
stages.hint: Tell the cat another tale in the library.

stages.journal: Three tales are in three books. The cat thanked us warmly, winked out, and left us rested in a way that feels borrowed. Something about the thanks did not sit right.
The cat is dead. His borrowed man's voice is gone from the world, and whoever it was stolen from can speak again.
The cat took his true shape and slipped out through the window, still wearing a stolen voice. He is out in the night somewhere, and he has not forgotten us.
stages.hint: Wisp has gone. If he turns up again, put an end to him.
